title: Hardware Tuning Profiles Pack — Rollout Monitoring Plan (SRE working doc)
body:
Owner: Aisha (SRE Dashboards)
Last updated: 2025-12-07
Status: Draft / in-flight with Runtime + Infra

Context
- We are rolling out the Hardware Tuning Profiles Pack (H100/L40S generally available; B200 gated/experimental) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private pools.
- Profiles change runtime scheduler/batching defaults, kernel-selection heuristics, and KV-cache/memory guardrails.
- SRE goal: detect regressions quickly (latency, errors, OOMs, tail behavior, streaming stability), keep oncall actions simple, and provide a clear rollback playbook by pool/region.

Non-goals (for this doc)
- Not a re-statement of the whole rollout runbook. This is monitoring + alert thresholds + readiness checks.
- Not a performance guarantee. We monitor “expected behavior” vs baseline and trigger rollback when we exceed guardrails.

Definitions / assumptions
- “Baseline” = current stable runtime in the same pool/region on the same model set, prior to profile enablement.
- “Canary” = profile-enabled subset of traffic within a pool/region, segmented by GPU SKU.
- “Pool” = a unit of capacity in Hosted/Dedicated (e.g., prod-us-east-h100-01). Infra owns canonical naming.
- Comparison window: last 30–60 minutes canary vs last 24 hours baseline for the same day-of-week/diurnal band where possible.
- Primary SLO signals: p50/p95 end-to-end latency, error rate, streaming stability, and request aborts/retries.

Rollout stages (monitoring gates)
Stage 0 — Pre-merge / pre-deploy
- Perf-canary gates in CI (Kira V / perf-canary). Required to pass for profile changes.
- Output artifact: workload matrix summary + gate status.
- SRE action: none unless gate noise >10% false fail rate (see “Noise control”).

Stage 1 — Shadow / no-op enablement
- Deploy runtime with profile selection/metrics enabled, but profile knobs not applied (or applied with “compat mode” to match baseline).
- Validate: profile selection metrics, override source correctness, SKU detection normalization.
- Gate: 0 critical alerts; profile selection unknown <0.1% of requests.

Stage 2 — Pool canary
- 1–5% traffic in a pool/region per SKU (H100, L40S). B200 only if experimental flag enabled + explicit approval.
- Minimum canary duration: 60 minutes OR 10k requests (whichever longer), excluding first 10 minutes warmup.
- Gate: no SEV2+ signals, no sustained p95 regressions over thresholds below.

Stage 3 — Expanded canary
- 25% traffic in pool/region.
- Gate: same as Stage 2; additionally ensure no capacity/queue instability and no increase in oncall pages.

Stage 4 — Full pool rollout
- 100% in pool/region.
- Gate: stable for 24 hours; then proceed to next region/pool.

Region ordering recommendation (Hosted)
- Start with low-blast-radius pools + stable diurnal patterns.
- Suggested: us-east → us-west → eu-central.
- Explicit: keep eu-west B200 disabled until experimental maturity improves (see incident thread 1764395502 + PR-22059).

Key dashboards (must exist before Stage 2)
1) “Hardware Profile Rollout Overview” (top-level)
- Traffic split (control vs canary), by pool/region, by GPU SKU
- Selected profile name + profile version, override source
- End-to-end latency (p50/p95/p99)
- Error rate and error codes (4xx/5xx, upstream timeouts)
- Abort/retry rates

2) “Scheduler Health”
- Queue depth / time-in-queue
- Batch size distribution
- Backpressure events / shed reasons
- Prefill vs decode time breakdown (if available)

3) “GPU + Memory Health”
- GPU utilization, SM occupancy proxy
- HBM used / fragmentation proxy (where instrumented)
- OOM events, CUDA errors
- KV-cache eviction / cache hit rate (if enabled)

4) “Streaming Stability”
- Stream disconnect rate
- Token gap/jitter (p95 inter-chunk time) if we have it
- Time-to-first-token and completion rate

5) “Profile Debug / Config Drift”
- Effective config dump sampling (CLI tool usage noted in PR-22066)
- Runtime startup logs: profile compatibility matrix (PR-22041)

Primary alerting philosophy
- Default to fast rollback, not “tune through a page.” If a profile causes a tail regression at canary, revert profile in that pool and open a follow-up issue.
- Alerts should page only on sustained issues AND only during an active canary window unless the issue is clearly customer-impacting.
- All alerts must be routable by pool/region/SKU to avoid global paging.

Alert thresholds (initial proposal)
Notes:
- Thresholds are relative-to-baseline where possible to reduce false positives.
- “Sustained” = 10 minutes unless otherwise specified.
- For Dedicated enterprise pools with strict SLOs, consider tighter p95 deltas (coord with Account/Solutions as needed).

A) Latency regression (page)
- Condition: p95 E2E latency (canary) > baseline p95 * 1.15 sustained 10m AND canary request count >= 500 in window
- Or: absolute p95 exceeds pool SLO threshold (if configured per pool) for 10m
- Action: rollback profile in pool (disable profile / revert to baseline profile version) and notify Runtime + Infra

B) Tail latency blow-up (page)
- Condition: p99 E2E latency (canary) > baseline p99 * 1.25 sustained 5m
- Action: immediate rollback; collect debug bundle (selected profile metric + effective config dump + scheduler stats)

C) Error rate / retries (page)
- Condition: 5xx rate (canary) > max( baseline 5xx + 0.3pp, baseline * 2 ) sustained 10m
- Condition: request retry rate (canary) > baseline * 1.5 sustained 10m
- Action: rollback; check CUDA errors / OOM / timeouts; open incident if impact is cross-pool

D) OOM / CUDA errors (page)
- Condition: OOM events > 0.2% of requests in canary over 10m OR > 5 OOMs / host / 10m
- Condition: CUDA error count non-zero sustained 5m (or spikes > 3/minute)
- Action: rollback immediately; if L40S, ensure KV budget guardrail is enabled; capture model + seq len distribution info from workload

E) Queue / backpressure instability (ticket + optional page if severe)
- Condition: time-in-queue p95 > baseline * 1.3 sustained 15m
- Condition: backpressure/shed events > baseline * 2 sustained 10m
- Page if also correlated with p95 regression or elevated 5xx.
- Action: rollback or reduce canary percent; coordinate with Scheduling team

F) Streaming stability (page for Hosted; ticket for Dedicated/Private unless enterprise-impact)
- Condition: stream disconnect rate > baseline * 2 sustained 10m
- Condition: TTFT p95 > baseline * 1.2 sustained 10m (streaming endpoints)
- Action: rollback; check scheduler fairness knobs and chunking behavior

G) Profile selection correctness (ticket)
- Condition: profile_selected = “unknown” > 0.1% requests over 30m
- Condition: override_source = “env” or “manual” unexpectedly spikes (possible misconfig)
- Action: stop rollout until detection normalization fixed; coordinate with Infra (SKU string variants)

Noise control / anti-flap rules
- During canary, alerts should evaluate only if request volume is sufficient (min counts above).
- Suppress pages during planned rollout steps (first 10 minutes) unless hard errors (OOM/CUDA) occur.
- Use burn-rate-like approach for latency (sustained over 10m) rather than single-minute spikes.
- If a pool is known noisy (e.g., flaky runners on L40S per INT-8832), do not use it for gating until fixed.

Operational readiness checklist (must be green before Stage 2)
Instrumentation
- [ ] Selected profile + profile_version metric emitted (PR-22027)
- [ ] Override source metric emitted (fleet default vs deployment override vs route/customer)
- [ ] GPU SKU normalization verified in-prod logs (H100 variants, PCIe vs SXM strings)
- [ ] Runtime startup log includes compatibility matrix (PR-22041)
- [ ] Debug endpoint/CLI for effective config available to oncall (PR-22066)

Dashboards
- [ ] Rollout overview dashboard with control vs canary compare panels
- [ ] Latency panels segmented by: model family, streaming/non-streaming, seq-len bucket (where available)
- [ ] Error panel includes top error codes + CUDA/OOM breakdown
- [ ] Queue/batching health panel exists (batch size histograms, queue time)

Alert routing + runbooks
- [ ] Alerts route to eng-oncall with pool/region labels
- [ ] Runbook section: “disable profiles per pool” is verified and fast (<5 minutes)
- [ ] Rollback criteria are explicit (see thresholds) and authorized (no extra approvals needed for safety rollback)

Infra / rollout controls
- [ ] Per-pool toggle exists (enable/disable profile pack)
- [ ] Ability to pin profile pack version per pool
- [ ] Ability to force baseline profile / safe profile if detection is ambiguous
- [ ] B200 experimental flag default OFF everywhere; allowlist pools only

Comms
- [ ] Oncall heads-up before Stage 2 in a new region
- [ ] Dedicated/Private support readiness: short FAQ on “what changed” + “how to revert”

Rollback triggers (summary for oncall)
Rollback immediately if any of:
- OOM/CUDA errors exceed thresholds
- p99 regression > 25% sustained 5m
- 5xx doubles vs baseline sustained 10m
- Streaming disconnect rate doubles sustained 10m (Hosted)

Rollback procedure (high level)
- Disable profile in affected pool (or revert profile version to last known good).
- Verify selected_profile metric returns to baseline within 5–10 minutes.
- Confirm latency/error metrics recover within 15–30 minutes.
- If not recovering: escalate to Runtime + Infra; consider rolling back runtime build.

B200 special handling
- B200 profiles are experimental and should be treated as “opt-in canary only.”
- Requirements:
  - Explicit driver/CUDA version checks must pass.
  - Rollout only in allowlisted pools with known-good topology.
  - Hard rollback threshold is stricter: any sustained p95 regression > 10% OR any non-trivial error increase triggers disable.
- Historical note: EU-West pool regression led to disable hotfix (PR-22059). Do not re-enable without a postmortem + sign-off.

Known gotchas (for alert triage)
- Tail latency regression can present as stable p50 but p95/p99 increases; often correlated with prefill/decode fairness settings.
- L40S: long-context workloads can trigger KV-cache pressure/fragmentation; watch OOM + retries + queue time.
- Mis-detection of SKU strings can silently select wrong profile; always check selected_profile + override_source first.

Open questions / TODOs
- TODO: Confirm pool naming conventions and label keys (Infra to provide canonical list).
- TODO: Decide final p95 delta thresholds per deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). Current proposal is one-size-fits-most.
- TODO: Add explicit “cost regressions” monitoring (tokens/sec per GPU-hour proxy) without paging (ticket-only).
- TODO: Define an “exit criteria” template per region (Talia wants a simple green checklist for the release checklist doc).

Change log
- 2025-11-22: Initial draft created after SRE request for concrete rollback thresholds.
- 2025-12-01: Added profile selection correctness metrics + anti-flap rules.
- 2025-12-07: Added B200 special handling notes + EU-West disable reference; tightened OOM paging criteria.
